description_full: UiPath, Inc. provides an automation platform that offers a range of robotic process automation (RPA) solutions primarily in the United States, Romania, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and internationally. It offers the UiPath platform, an integrated enterprise software platform that enables AI agents, robots, people, and models to work together in coordinated workflows. The company's UiPath platform includes the UiPath Maestro process orchestration and process intelligence; UiPath agent builder; RPA and API automation; UiPath intelligent xtraction and processing; UiPath test cloud for testing and quality assurance; UiPath packaged and prebuilt agentic solutions; and centralized governance capabilities that apply across automations, AI agents, and manual tasks. It serves the financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, and public sectors. The company was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: UiPath, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.8B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +14.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -110% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $352M in free cash flow — roughly 22 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.31× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 18% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 10% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
